result.text: Title: Robotic Burger Seller near the University of Vienna The robot receives an order.
It asks whether the customer wants a menu or just the burger.
If he wants a menu, the robot starts preparing the drink, which depending on the size can take a variable amount of time.
While doing so, he asks if you want fries or wedges.
If you want fries, he prepares the fries; if you want wedges, he prepares wedges.
Again the duration varies depending on the size fries/wedges order.
After that, he prepares the burger, and gives you enthusiastic status updates every 30 seconds.
Depending on the number of ingredients, the duration for creating the burger varies.
Your order is delivered via a conveyor belt.

result.rule: Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description presents process activities in a stated order: Model the corresponding flow nodes in that order with sequence flows, connecting the start event to the initial activity and the final activity to the end event.

When the description presents activities whose execution order must be represented in BPMN: Represent that order with sequence flows that are direct children of the relevant process or subprocess scope; do not place sequence flows inside activities or other BPMN elements.

When the description says an occurrence may or may not happen and that its occurrence changes what the process does: Represent the possible occurrence with an appropriate BPMN event or decision gateway, and connect the path for handling it with sequence flows.

When the description says that a sequence of work must happen before the process proceeds to other described work: Model that sequence as connected to the main process flow, with its completion leading to the subsequent work, rather than as a detached start-to-end chain.

When the description states a condition that determines which alternative path is taken: Label the corresponding BPMN gateway with that stated condition, rather than with an adjacent activity or a downstream outcome.

When the description assigns different actions to distinct ranges or levels of a measured value: Model a decision gateway with conditional outgoing flows that lead to the action for each range or level.
